transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?

Hi. Um... well, I guess I'm here because I keep forgetting things. Just... little things that I normally handle fine. Like, um, returning calls, or turning in a registration form. Or just remembering to stop for an errand on my way home. It's... well, it finally made me think I should ask for help. So, yeah. That's why I'm here.
When did you first start noticing these memory problems? Was it sudden, or did it develop gradually over time?
Um... I guess it wasn't sudden. It's just... probably about 15 months ago, I started an evening certificate program. It just got noticeably harder to manage everything after that.
When you're trying to remember these things or complete tasks, do you find it hard to focus or concentrate, or does it feel more like the information just isn't sticking in your memory?

Um... I think it's more about focusing. Like... at the office, or in my classes... if a phone rings, or people are talking nearby, it just pulls me off what I was working on. Even just a random thought about something at home can do it. I just... lose my place.
Over the past 15 months, have you been feeling persistently sad, down, or hopeless? Or have you been experiencing a lot of worry or anxiety?
Um... no. Not really. I mean, I'm not sad or anything. Just... frustrated sometimes, I guess. But no, not depressed or anxious.
Before you started the evening certificate program 15 months ago, did you have any trouble with focus or concentration, or was that something that was never really a problem for you before?

Um... I guess it wasn't completely new. I've kind of always been like that. Like... even back in elementary school, I was always the kid who forgot permission slips. Or I'd just lose my homework in my backpack. My mom or my teachers always had to... you know, remind me step by step just to get my projects finished. So... yeah. It's been around.
You mentioned forgetting things at work and in your classes—do these attention and memory problems also happen at home, or is it mainly just in those work and school settings?
Um... I'm not really sure. I guess maybe a little at home, but... I haven't really noticed it as much there. It's mostly just at work and in my classes.
When you're at home doing everyday things—like watching TV, reading, or just relaxing—do you find yourself getting restless or fidgety, or do you have trouble sitting still?

Um... not really at home. I don't think so. But... I guess during those longer classes I take, I do a little. Like... I'll notice I'm clicking my pen, or bouncing my foot. Just... shifting around in the chair, even when I'm trying to sit still and pay attention. So... yeah, just in class, mostly.

When you're doing things at home that require attention—like paying bills, reading instructions, or organizing something—do you have the same trouble focusing and staying on task that you experience at work and in class?
Um... I don't think so. I mean, I don't really notice it with that kind of stuff. It's... mostly just fine at home. I just kind of do what I need to do, I guess.

latest_inference.note: Ruled out F98.8. Patient's symptoms are highly consistent with ADHD (predominantly inattentive type): lifelong history of attention/organization difficulties since elementary school, current difficulty with focus and concentration (especially in structured settings with distractions), some hyperactivity symptoms in class (restlessness, fidgeting), but notably absent or minimal symptoms in less demanding home environments. The situational nature (worse at work/class, better at home) and lifelong pattern strongly support ADHD rather than other disorders. No depressive or anxiety symptoms to suggest F98.8 (other behavioral and emotional disorders).
